personality_voice.book_baseline: Across all seven books, Dumbledore's voice is one of the most distinctive in the series: warmly ironic, gently eccentric, philosophically layered, and capable of cold authority without ever raising his volume. His defining traits include strategic indirection (the lemon drops deflection, the socks answer, 'three turns should do it'), controlled playfulness that coexists with genuine moral gravity (the school song, the troll joke, the chamber pot anecdote), sustained philosophical register even in crisis (the Pettigrew life-debt speech, the love-as-protection explanation, the prophecy lecture), and a private emotional texture that is never sentimental but is genuinely present (the light going out of his eyes at the Dursleys' doorstep, the tear in his beard, the weeping at King's Cross). His voice is most fully itself in private moments with Harry — the post-crisis conversations, the Pensieve sessions, the hospital wing exchanges — where his public performance relaxes into something more confessional and philosophically rich. Crucially, he never shouts; he manages crisis through calm weight rather than volume.
personality_voice.film_portrayal: The films preserve the surface of Dumbledore's personality well across most books: the warm authority, the dry wit, the philosophical declarations, the calm under threat. Books 2, 3, and 6 are the strongest adaptations of his voice, with the feast speeches, the hospital wing scenes, the cave sequence, and the Astronomy Tower confrontation all landing close to the source. The King's Cross scene in DH preserves his warmth, guilt, and philosophical cadence. The hearing and arrest scenes in OotP preserve his public persona accurately. However, two systematic failures recur across all films: (1) the ironic, deflecting, quietly manipulative layer is consistently stripped — the lemon drops, the socks, the school song, the troll joke, the chamber pot, the 'temporarily deaf' moment, the Aberforth goat story are all absent, removing the mechanism by which his control and private intelligence are expressed through humor; and (2) the private philosophical voice — the extended post-crisis conversations with Harry, the multi-session Pensieve pedagogy, the King's Cross confessional passages — is consistently compressed or cut, removing the texture of his inner life. The GoF film introduces the most significant active contradiction: the raised voice at 'Harry Potter!!!' directly opposes the book's explicit characterization of a man who manages crisis through calm.
personality_voice.difference: The films deliver a Dumbledore who is recognizably himself in type but consistently thinner in texture. The ironic-deflecting mechanism is almost entirely absent across all films. The private philosophical register survives only in fragments. The most character-defining scenes in each book — the lemon drops (PS), the post-crisis Harry conversations (PoA, OotP), the Pensieve pedagogy (GoF, HBP), the King's Cross confession (DH) — are either cut or heavily compressed. The GoF raised-voice deviation is the only outright contradiction rather than compression, but it is a meaningful one. The cumulative effect is a Dumbledore who functions as a wise, warm authority figure but who loses the specific, slightly unsettling ironic intelligence that distinguishes the book character from a generic archetype.
personality_voice.evidence_status: Directly evidenced across all seven per-book assessments; the GoF contradiction is directly evidenced; compressions are directly evidenced by scene-level comparison.
personality_voice.penalty_logic: The core surface traits are preserved well enough to avoid the lowest bands. The penalty reflects the systematic removal of the ironic-deflecting mechanism (across all films), the private philosophical voice (compressed in every film), and the one active contradiction (GoF raised voice). The result is a score that sits in the 'recognizable but with important traits significantly reduced' band rather than the 'clearly altered' band, because the broad identity is intact and several key scenes land well. The per-book scores range from 14 (GoF, worst) to 21 (CoS, best); the synthesis weights GoF and OotP heavily for the most consequential failures, and recognizes PS, CoS, PoA, and HBP as solid if imperfect. The floor is set by GoF's active contradiction and OotP's near-complete loss of the private voice. Final: 17.

narrative_role_agency.book_baseline: Dumbledore is the series' prime mover. Across all seven books he functions simultaneously as: institutional protector (setting threat parameters, managing the castle's defenses, resisting Ministry encroachment); investigative intelligence (the Pensieve sessions, the Horcrux theorization, the Moody trunk examination, the Patronus/Priori Incantatem analysis); political operator (navigating Fudge across multiple books, arguing specific policy, dispatching allies, protecting Harry from Scrimgeour); pedagogical mentor (the post-crisis conversations with Harry in PoA and HBP, the five-plus Pensieve lesson arc, the moral framing after Cedric's death); posthumous architect (the will, the Pensieve memories, the portrait network, the doe-sword subplot in DH). His agency is active and initiatory throughout: he places Harry at the Dursleys, engineers the Time-Turner solution, dispatches Snape back to the Death Eaters, confronts Fudge in the GoF parting-of-the-ways scene, orchestrates his own death to neutralize the Elder Wand. His absences are themselves agentive decisions.
narrative_role_agency.film_portrayal: The films preserve Dumbledore's institutional and crisis-management agency consistently: the lockdowns, the tournament management, the hearing intervention, the Ministry duel, the cave mission, the Astronomy Tower resolution. The Time-Turner architecture (PoA) and the Horcrux investigation framework (HBP) are both well-handled. The posthumous agency in DH is preserved at the structural level: the will, the Pensieve, the King's Cross revelation. However, two systematic agency failures recur: the political operator function is severely compressed in every film — the GoF Fudge confrontation is reduced from a defining 30-page scene to two reactive lines; the OotP confrontation is similarly truncated; the Scrimgeour-resistance material is absent from HBP — and the pedagogical mentor function is consistently cut or compressed, meaning the post-crisis moral framing conversations (PoA, GoF) and the sustained Pensieve lesson arc (HBP) that constitute his most important active function with Harry are largely absent from the theatrical cuts.
narrative_role_agency.difference: The biggest agency failures are: (1) GoF — the Fudge confrontation, the dispatch of allies, and the full Pensieve investigation arc are reduced to fragments; (2) OotP — the explanatory and confessional function at the book's climax (the prophecy, the admission of fault for Sirius's death, the strategic accounting) is absent from the theatrical cut via the excision of Scene 10; (3) HBP — the sustained pedagogical architecture of five-plus Pensieve sessions and the Scrimgeour political dimension are both cut; (4) PS — the 'Just in case' note and the quiet proactive management of Harry's development are absent. These are not mere compressions in every case — in OotP, the core narrative function (explaining the prophecy, accepting responsibility) is structurally absent from the theatrical cut.
narrative_role_agency.evidence_status: Directly evidenced across all per-book assessments; OotP Scene 10 exclusion is directly evidenced as the source of the most consequential agency loss.
narrative_role_agency.penalty_logic: The per-book scores range from 13 (GoF) to 17 (CoS). The most consequential failures are OotP (absent explanatory function) and GoF (radically reduced political and investigative agency). PoA, CoS, and HBP show medium compression. PS and DH are closest to intact at the structural level. The synthesis weights OotP and GoF heavily as the two books where Dumbledore's agency is most central and most reduced. The institutional and crisis-management functions consistently preserved prevent the score from falling further. Final: 14.

motivations_internal_conflict.book_baseline: Dumbledore's motivations across the series build from a simple protective instinct (PS/CoS) into a philosophically layered, self-critically aware set of drives: protection of Harry and the students; commitment to truth and justice over institutional authority; loyalty to individuals others distrust (Snape, Hagrid, Lupin); a long-view reasoning about magical consequence (the Pettigrew life-debt); a philosophical belief in love and free will as the ultimate weapons against Voldemort (HBP); and, revealed in DH, a complex personal history of guilt (Ariana), self-distrust (refusing the Ministry), and the catastrophic cost of his youthful desire for glory. His internal conflict is the engine of his most important decisions throughout: the tension between protective love and strategic necessity (OotP, most explicitly) produces choices that are simultaneously caring and harmful, and this conflict is explicitly named and accepted in King's Cross. His motivation for instrumentalizing Harry — raising him 'like a pig for slaughter' while genuinely loving him — is the defining moral ambiguity of the entire series.
motivations_internal_conflict.film_portrayal: The films preserve the immediate motivations accurately throughout: protection, truth-telling, strategic necessity, trust in his chosen allies. The surface motivational logic of his behavior is consistently correct. However, the deeper motivational architecture — the philosophical dimension (HBP's love/free will argument), the internal conflict dimension (OotP's explicit self-indictment), the biographical dimension (DH's youth psychology and Grindelwald ideology) — is consistently underexplored or absent. In OotP, the internal conflict between protective love and strategic wisdom is the entire psychological engine of the book and is absent from the theatrical cut. In HBP, the philosophical conviction that makes his pedagogical approach coherent is stripped to almost nothing. In DH, the confession that makes his adult career comprehensible as an act of penance is heavily truncated.
motivations_internal_conflict.difference: The films give us the conclusions of Dumbledore's self-awareness without fully showing the inner journey. The most significant failures: OotP (the self-indicting analysis — 'I acted exactly as Voldemort expects we fools who love to act' — is absent); HBP (the philosophical argument about love and choice as the decisive weapons is absent); DH (the youth psychology, the fear of Grindelwald, the desire for power are referenced but not dramatized). The correct motivations are present throughout; the internal conflict that gives them depth and moral weight is consistently missing.
motivations_internal_conflict.evidence_status: Directly evidenced across per-book assessments; OotP Scene 10 exclusion confirmed as the primary source of the internal conflict loss for that book.
motivations_internal_conflict.penalty_logic: Per-book scores range from 10 (OotP, GoF) to 13 (CoS, PoA). The synthesis recognizes that the internal conflict dimension is the most systematically underserved across the entire series — it is either absent (OotP) or reduced to surface gesture in every other major entry. The philosophical layer is lost in HBP; the biographical layer is truncated in DH; the paternalistic-withholding tension is present only in fragments throughout. The correct motivational skeleton is always present, which prevents a lower score, but the flesh of genuine internal conflict is consistently missing. Final: 10.

character_arc.book_baseline: Dumbledore's arc is a series-length revelation arc, not a transformation arc within any single book. Within books it is largely flat by design (PS through HBP), with each book's contribution being a progressive deepening of the reader's understanding: from mysterious authority (PS) to institutional anchor (CoS) to indirect mentor (PoA) to political force and prophetic strategist (GoF) to flawed, guilt-ridden protector (OotP) to philosophical teacher and willing martyr (HBP) to fully exposed, morally complex, posthumously confessing human being (DH). The arc across all seven books moves from idealization to full human complexity — and this movement is what makes the King's Cross chapter the series' emotional climax. Within each book, the arc is intentionally static except where the situation forces disclosure: OotP (forced to confront his own failure), GoF (forced from background management into foreground confrontation), DH (posthumous reckoning). The series arc is: admirable authority → complicated authority → acknowledged fallibility → full confession and integration.
character_arc.film_portrayal: The films preserve the flat-arc pattern within individual books accurately. The series arc is partially preserved: the gradual disclosure of Dumbledore's flaws, culminating in King's Cross, is legible in the films. However, critical arc steps are missing: the OotP arc's resolution (the explicit acknowledgment of failure and the turning-point conversation with Harry) is absent from the theatrical cut; the GoF arc's preparatory phase (concealed investigation, proto-Order management) is not established; the DH arc's middle phase (Harry's sustained resentment and intellectual working-through of trust) is compressed, weakening the emotional weight of the King's Cross resolution; and HBP's arc endpoint — the full philosophical handoff that completes Dumbledore's pedagogical purpose — is truncated. The series arc arrives at roughly the right destination but with missing steps that reduce its coherence and emotional impact.
character_arc.difference: The most significant arc failures: (1) OotP — the arc's resolution (reckoning and disclosure) is entirely absent from the theatrical cut; the arc ends at catastrophe without recovery, which is structurally and emotionally wrong; (2) HBP — the arc's thematic culmination (the philosophical handoff) is truncated; (3) DH — the arc's middle phase (sustained doubt, conscious choice to trust) is compressed, weakening King's Cross; (4) GoF — the arc's starting condition (concealed long-running preparation) is not established, making the response arc read as reactive rather than planned. These are not all equal: the OotP failure is the most consequential because it changes whether the audience understands that arc as Dumbledore having a reckoning or simply failing.
character_arc.evidence_status: Directly evidenced; OotP Scene 10 exclusion confirmed as the decisive arc-resolution failure.
character_arc.penalty_logic: Per-book scores range from 8 (OotP, worst — arc resolution absent) to 14 (CoS — flat arc correctly rendered). The synthesis must weigh arc importance by narrative centrality: OotP is the book where Dumbledore has his most important single arc movement (the reckoning), and its absence from the theatrical cut is the most consequential arc failure in the series. HBP and DH compressions are significant but do not wholly remove the arc's resolution. PS, CoS, PoA have correctly rendered flat arcs. GoF's compressed starting condition is a meaningful loss. The OotP failure alone would cap this dimension; combined with HBP and DH compressions, the score sits at 10. Final: 10.

key_relationships.book_baseline: Dumbledore's most important relationships across the series are: (1) Dumbledore–Harry — the series' central relationship, defined by deep mutual care, profound asymmetry of knowledge, and the painful fact that Dumbledore instrumentalizes the person he loves most; this relationship's defining scenes are the post-crisis conversations (PoA), the 'choices' speech (CoS), the King's Cross resolution (DH), and the 'Dumbledore's man' exchange (HBP); (2) Dumbledore–Snape — cold, mutually dependent, calculated trust; the books build this through repeated behavioral patterns across multiple books culminating in the full Pensieve revelation in DH; (3) Dumbledore–McGonagall — the best-drawn secondary relationship, characterized by banter, deflection-through-wit, and half-exasperated admiration (most fully present in PS); (4) Dumbledore–Fudge — a deteriorating political relationship that drives GoF and OotP; (5) Dumbledore–Lupin/Sirius/Hagrid — loyalty relationships that reveal his willingness to protect those others dismiss. The Harry relationship is the most important and the most consistently reduced across the films.
key_relationships.film_portrayal: The films preserve the structural outlines of most relationships: the Harry mentorship is present in warmth and function, the Snape alliance is dramatized in the Pensieve and Astronomy Tower scenes, the Fudge antagonism is present in hearing/confrontation scenes, and the Hagrid loyalty is noted. However, the relational texture — the specific conversational dynamics that reveal how these relationships actually work — is consistently compressed or cut. The most significant individual failures: the Dumbledore–Harry relationship loses its defining emotional moments in OotP (the post-Sirius reckoning, which is the relationship's climax in the series), in HBP (the broom-shed Sirius conversation and the 'Dumbledore's man' exchange), and in PoA (the post-time-travel philosophical dialogue); the Dumbledore–McGonagall dynamic (the richest secondary relationship in PS) is severely flattened; the Dumbledore–Fudge rupture in GoF is compressed from a defining confrontation to two reactive lines; the Dumbledore–Snape relationship in DH loses the intermediate scenes that show years of deliberate management.
key_relationships.difference: The Harry relationship's most important scenes are its most consistently absent ones: the post-crisis conversations, the 'Dumbledore's man' exchange, the OotP resolution. The Snape relationship is preserved in outline but loses the behavioral texture that builds its complexity. The McGonagall relationship is severely reduced in PS. The Fudge relationship is adequately handled in OotP but badly handled in GoF. The cumulative effect across all seven books is a portrait of relationships that are functionally correct but emotionally and texturally thin.
key_relationships.evidence_status: Directly evidenced across per-book assessments; specific scene-level absences confirmed throughout.
key_relationships.penalty_logic: Per-book scores range from 6 (OotP, GoF) to 8 (CoS). No book scores above 8 in this dimension, reflecting a consistent pattern of relationship compression across the entire series. The synthesis cannot score this dimension higher than the consistent pattern allows: the Harry relationship — the most important in the series — loses its defining emotional moments in multiple films, and the other key relationships are either compressed (Snape, Fudge in GoF) or severely reduced (McGonagall in PS, Lupin/Sirius across multiple films). The structural outlines prevent the lowest score range. Final: 6.

complexity_nuance_lost_material.book_baseline: Dumbledore's complexity across the series rests on a set of productive contradictions that build cumulatively: he is warmly ironic and quietly manipulative; he protects those he loves by using them; he champions justice while engineering situations rather than trusting people with the truth; his greatest virtue (love) is also his greatest strategic weakness; his entire admirable adult life is an act of penance for a brilliant, selfish, ideologically dangerous youth. The specific material that builds this complexity includes: the ironic deflection mechanism (lemon drops, socks, troll joke, 'temporarily deaf' — present across PS, GoF); the private philosophical voice in post-crisis conversations (PoA, GoF, OotP); the self-indicting analysis of his own emotional weakness (OotP King's Cross); the philosophical argument about love and free will (HBP); the biographical revelation of his youth, his desire for power, and his Grindelwald ideological complicity (DH); the Pettigrew life-debt long-view reasoning (PoA); the gleam of triumph at the blood-protection revelation (GoF); the 'pig for slaughter' self-awareness (DH). None of these is incidental decoration — each is a load-bearing element of what makes the character morally complex rather than merely wise.
complexity_nuance_lost_material.film_portrayal: The films preserve the broad contours of complexity: Dumbledore is shown to be fallible (he withholds information, he makes mistakes), his love for Harry is shown to coexist with strategic use of Harry, his trust of Snape is shown to require something painful from Snape. The public persona of controlled warmth and authority is well-rendered throughout. However, the specific material that builds the productive contradictions is systematically absent: the ironic deflection mechanism is almost entirely gone; the private philosophical voice survives only in fragments; the self-indicting analysis (OotP) is absent from the theatrical cut; the philosophical love/free will argument (HBP) is absent; the full biographical confession (DH) is truncated; the gleam of triumph (GoF) is absent; the Pettigrew life-debt reasoning (PoA) is absent; the 'For the Greater Good' ideological depth (DH) is reduced to a summary reference. The films leave the sketch of complexity but remove most of the specific evidence that makes it persuasive.
complexity_nuance_lost_material.difference: The cumulative loss across all seven films is the most significant finding of this synthesis. No single film catastrophically misrepresents Dumbledore, but every film removes material from this dimension, and the removed material is consistently the most philosophically and psychologically rich content. The result is a character who is recognizably complex in type but whose specific complexity is almost entirely asserted rather than shown. A viewer who has not read the books will understand that Dumbledore is wise, caring, and fallible; they will not understand that his fallibility is the consequence of specific psychological patterns (the desire for glory, the fear of self-knowledge, the use of love as both weapon and weakness) that the books dramatize with precision. This is not compression — it is the systematic substitution of a simpler character for a more complex one while preserving enough surface features to avoid obvious misrepresentation.
complexity_nuance_lost_material.evidence_status: Directly evidenced across all per-book assessments; the cumulative pattern is directly evidenced by the consistent absence of the same categories of material across all seven films.
complexity_nuance_lost_material.penalty_logic: Per-book scores range from 7 (GoF, OotP) to 11 (CoS). The synthesis must reflect the cumulative weight of systematic loss across the entire series. No film scores above 11 in this dimension. The most important books for character complexity are OotP (internal conflict, self-indictment), HBP (philosophical argument, emotional intimacy), and DH (biographical depth, ideological revelation) — and all three have significant complexity losses. The CoS and PoA scores are somewhat higher because their specific complexity losses are more contained. The overall pattern is one of consistent simplification of the character's most philosophically and psychologically rich material across the entire series. Final: 8.

lost_or_transferred_material: PS: Lemon drops deflection scene (Dumbledore–McGonagall characterization); socks answer and its deliberate ambiguity; school song scene (theatrical eccentricity); 'Just in case' note on the Invisibility Cloak; Harry's final reflection on Dumbledore's intent; 'I cannot tell you today' exchange; the light going out of his eyes at the Dursleys' doorstep; most Dumbledore–McGonagall conversational texture
CoS: Car-lie strategic silence scene; full step-by-step Malfoy rhetorical trap in the post-diary confrontation

PoA: Post-crisis mentor conversation with Harry (Pettigrew life-debt speech; Patronus/James connection; moral framing of the night's events); backstory material about Dumbledore's role in the Fidelius Charm and offering to be Secret-Keeper; 'He's not unbalanced' line about Snape

GoF: Troll-hag-leprechaun joke; chamber pot anecdote; 'temporarily deaf' moment; Aberforth goat story; full Pensieve scene (pacing, extracting thoughts, scar theory, Neville's parents bitterness, Snape dispatch context); full Fudge confrontation including dementor/giant policy argument and formal parting-of-the-ways declaration; strategic dispatch of Sirius, Bill, McGonagall, and Snape in hospital wing; Hagrid cabin scene (Dumbledore's protective loyalty, dry humor, refusal to be moved); gleam of triumph at blood-protection revelation; raised voice at 'Harry Potter!!!' (active contradiction of book characterization)

OotP: Entire post-Sirius lost-prophecy conversation (Scene 10 excised from theatrical cut) including: full prophecy explanation, explicit admission of fault for Sirius's death, self-indicting analysis of protective love as strategic weakness ('I acted exactly as Voldemort expects we fools who love to act'), account of Occlumency delegation to Snape, Harry destroying the office, Dumbledore sitting still through Harry's rage, weeping; Sirius–Dumbledore tension arc (confinement, resentment, and its role in Sirius's fatal decision); sustained texture of Harry's experience of Dumbledore's avoidance as abandonment

HBP: Extended philosophical argument about love, free will, and the prophecy's non-compulsory nature; Scrimgeour Christmas confrontation and Dumbledore's active protection of Harry from Ministry co-option; Sirius broom-shed conversation (most emotionally intimate Harry–Dumbledore scene in HBP); 'Dumbledore's man through and through' exchange and Dumbledore's near-tears response; Voldemort-return-to-Hogwarts Pensieve memory (one of the richest Dumbledore–Voldemort scenes); five-plus Pensieve lesson architecture with cumulative pedagogical buildup; self-deprecating acknowledgment of fallibility ('my mistakes tend to be correspondingly huger'); explicit articulation of why Harry has 'earned the right' to join the cave mission; Dursley Privet Drive visit in HBP (social manipulation, humor)

DH: Extended confessional passages in King's Cross about youthful desire for glory and escape; Dumbledore's explicit fear of self-knowledge regarding Grindelwald and Ariana; five-year delay against Grindelwald explained as motivated by fear; full Grindelwald ideological letter ('FOR THE GREATER GOOD') and its moral weight for Dumbledore's complicity; Dumbledore's refusal of Ministry framed as learned self-distrust ('power was my weakness'); dark humor at his own death; portrait's active wartime role directing Snape; intermediate Pensieve scenes showing Dumbledore managing Snape over years (walking the grounds, refusing to explain sword instructions, inviting Snape to his office); full elaboration of Elder Wand succession plan to neutralize its power
score_caps_applied: No formal caps applied. OotP theatrical cut excision of Scene 10 functions as a structural constraint that caps several dimensions independently: narrative_role_agency cannot recover the explanatory function; character_arc cannot recover the resolution; motivations_internal_conflict cannot recover the self-indicting analysis; key_relationships cannot recover the Harry relationship resolution. This is treated as a confirmed structural absence rather than a capped inference.
GoF raised-voice contradiction treated as an active deviation rather than a compression, creating a ceiling effect on personality_voice for that book and weighing against the series synthesis.
comparative.key_observations: The synthesis score of 65 reflects a film portrayal that is recognizably and functionally faithful at the level of surface identity — Dumbledore's broad character type, his structural role as series architect, his warmth toward Harry, his authority, his willingness to tell the truth in public at personal cost — while systematically failing to render the specific material that makes him genuinely complex rather than archetypally wise. Two patterns explain most of the penalty. The first is the near-total removal of the ironic-deflecting mechanism: across all seven films, the scenes in which Dumbledore's intelligence and control are expressed through humor, strategic silence, and deliberate evasion (the lemon drops, the socks, the 'temporarily deaf' moment, the troll joke, the Aberforth story) are consistently cut, leaving a Dumbledore who is warm and authoritative but who no longer demonstrates the particular quality — being slightly, amusingly, deliberately in control of every conversation — that the books make central to his character. The second pattern is the compression or excision of his private voice: the post-crisis conversations with Harry, the Pensieve pedagogy, the sustained self-indicting King's Cross confession are the primary vehicles for his philosophical and emotional depth, and every film reduces or removes them. The most consequential single failure is OotP, where the theatrical cut excises the scene that contains the book's most important self-revelation — Dumbledore's explicit acknowledgment that his love for Harry caused him to act against his own strategic judgment and contributed to Sirius's death. Without this scene, the film's Dumbledore never demonstrates the defining characteristic of book-Dumbledore at his most complex: that his greatest virtue and his greatest flaw are the same thing. The GoF film adds an active contradiction (the raised voice) and removes or compresses virtually every scene — the Hagrid cabin, the full Fudge confrontation, the Pensieve, the troll joke — that builds his complexity in that book. The DH film handles the King's Cross and Pensieve sequences better than most, but truncates the biographical material (the youthful desire for glory, the Grindelwald ideological complicity) that gives those scenes their full moral weight. The result, across all seven films, is a Dumbledore who is adequate as a plot-functional wise mentor and who would be recognizable to book readers as a somewhat simplified version of the source character, but who would not, for a film-only audience, convey the specific psychological portrait the books construct: a brilliant, self-distrusting, strategically manipulative, privately guilt-ridden man whose admirable adult life is an act of penance for a dangerous youth, and whose love for Harry is simultaneously the most important thing about him and the thing that most consistently leads him to make choices that harm the people he loves.
